title: Part Lifecycle update: questions from QA
intro: Hi Chris, these came up while we were writing the test cases for the Part Lifecycle update, using the spec page as it stood on 8 Oct (v26). Each row stands on its own. Put a letter, or your own answer, in the last column. None of them stop us working; your answers decide what a few of the tests check.

rows.now: Several of the Part Lifecycle stories (SV-10814 to SV-10826) still have older wording than the spec page. For example, some describe a separate canned job warning for each part, while the spec now has one warning that lists all of them. Some items in the spec are not in any story yet.
rows.question: Where they differ, should we test what the spec page says?
rows.options:
A) Yes, the spec page. The stories will be brought in line.
B) Yes, the spec page. The stories can stay as they are.
C) Some stories have newer decisions than the spec. I'll say which.
D) Not sure, check with the engineers.

rows.now:
A few design screens are older than the spec page:
1. The Inventory Value tooltip is missing the sentence the spec adds.
2. One screen still shows a separate pop-up for each part when a canned job is applied.
3. A note on the history screen puts "Changed at" in a different place from the spec.
4. A note says saving any untracked part needs Delete.
5. One screen makes the Staff, Date and Time columns narrower.
For now we test what the spec says.
rows.question: Is the spec page right on all five?
rows.options:
A) Yes, all five. The design will be updated.
B) The design is right on some of them. I'll say which.
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: Inventory list column name
rows.now: The design, and the Inventory list on staging today, label the quantity column "Total Quantity". The spec page, and your answer to the planning questions, say "Total Qty".
rows.question: Which label should the column have when this ships?
rows.options:
A) Total Qty
B) Total Quantity
C) Either is fine.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: adding a part number that already exists
rows.now: Adding a part number that is already stocked at the location is blocked with "<part number> already exists at this location." Part numbers match whatever the dashes, spaces and capitals, so a location can hold FF-5507 (active) and ff5507 (inactive) and both count as the same number.
rows.question: In that case, which spelling should the message show?
rows.options:
A) The active part's number (FF-5507).
B) The inactive part's number (ff5507).
C) The number the user typed.
D) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: changing a part's description
rows.now: When you change a part's description and the same part is stocked at other locations, the part window warns: "This also changes the description at 3 other locations." For the same warning on part numbers, the spec says inactive parts at other locations are counted. It says nothing either way for descriptions.
rows.question: Should inactive parts at other locations count in the description warning too?
rows.options:
A) Yes, count them, the same as for part numbers.
B) No, count only active parts.
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: Vendor field in the part window
rows.now: The spec says the Vendor field is hidden "where the screen that opens the dialog hides it". We couldn't work out which screen that means.
rows.question: Which screen opens the part window without the Vendor field?
rows.options:
A) This screen: (please name it)
B) None. Vendor always shows.
C) Not sure, check with the engineers.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: canned jobs that include an inactive part
rows.now: When a canned job is applied, inactive parts are left out and one warning lists them: "These parts are inactive and were not added: ...". In some canned jobs the vendor part number was typed in by hand, so it can be written slightly differently from the part it matches, for example FF5507 typed in the job and FF-5507 on the part.
rows.question: Which number should the warning show?
rows.options:
A) The number as typed in the canned job (FF5507).
B) The part's own number (FF-5507).
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: Part Library entry deleted in another tab
rows.now: Someone has a Part Library entry open in one browser tab and deletes it in another tab. Then they save a change in the first tab. The spec has two messages that could fit: "Failed to save library part." and "Part Library entry not found".
rows.question: Which message should they see?
rows.options:
A) Failed to save library part.
B) Part Library entry not found.
C) Either is fine.
D) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: message after a bulk change
rows.now: After a bulk change the message reads, for example, "2 parts updated." A part with a core charge also has its core, which shows as its own line.
rows.question: If you bulk-change 2 parts and both have a core, what should the message say?
rows.options:
A) 2 parts updated. (cores are not counted)
B) 4 parts updated. (each core counts)
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: Supply filter on the Inventory list
rows.now: The spec calls the first choice in the Supply filter "All". The Inventory list today shows "All categories".
rows.question: What should the first choice say after this release?
rows.options:
A) All
B) All categories
C) Either is fine.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: changing only the punctuation of a part number
rows.now: Part numbers match whatever the dashes, spaces, dots and capitals, so FF-5507 and FF5507 count as the same number. The spec also says saving a part with an unchanged number is never blocked.
rows.question: If someone edits a part from FF-5507 to FF5507 (only the dash removed) and no other part has that number, what should happen?
rows.options:
A) It saves. It is the same part.
B) It is blocked as a duplicate.
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: Inventory Value report after the negative stock fix (SV-10380)
rows.now: With the fix, the Inventory Value report counts bins that have gone below zero. A part with bins of 5 and minus 2 counts as 3, not 5. Figures saved for past dates were worked out the old way, counting only the positive bins.
rows.question: Should past dates keep the figures they were saved with, or be worked out again the new way?
rows.options:
A) Keep the saved figures for past dates.
B) Work out past dates again.
C) Not sure, check with the engineers.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: Critical Reorder list on the dashboard
rows.now: The spec says untracked and inactive parts are left out of the dashboard's Critical Reorder list. The Dashboard v1 plan replaces the current dashboard.
rows.question: When Part Lifecycle ships, will the Critical Reorder list still be on the dashboard?
rows.options:
A) Yes, keep testing it.
B) No, it will be gone by then. Drop those tests.
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: Inventory Value report fix (SV-10380)
rows.now: To test the fix we need a part whose bin has gone below zero, for example bins of 5 and minus 2.
rows.question: How does a bin go below zero in normal use, so a tester can set it up?
rows.options:
A) These steps: (please describe)
B) It can only be set up directly in the data.
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: turning tracking on for a part
rows.now: The spec covers two cases when tracking is turned on: a part with no bin location, and a part with bin locations but none set as the default. We need to set both up.
rows.question: How does a part end up with no bin location, or with no default bin?
rows.options:
A) These steps: (please describe)
B) Only through an import or old data.
C) Not sure.

rows.now: Some cases need the new global search to be on for the organisation.
rows.question: How is it switched on for an organisation?
rows.options:
A) A setting a tester can change: (please say where)
B) The developers switch it on.
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: deleting an inventory part
rows.now: Some cases need a Part Library entry that is no longer stocked anywhere.
rows.question: When an inventory part is deleted, does its Part Library entry stay?
rows.options:
A) Yes, it stays.
B) No, it is deleted too.
C) Not sure.

rows.topic: Part Lifecycle: seeing a part's core
rows.now: Some cases check what happens to a part's core (shown as "Core for ...").
rows.question: Where does a tester see a part's core in the app?
rows.options:
A) Here: (please say where)
B) Not sure.

internal: Stories SV-10814 to SV-10826 vs PRD v26
Document vs document mismatch: a question, never a defect (skill 07 section 5). Cases follow the PRD.
Document vs document mismatch. Cases follow the PRD.
Design and staging say Total Quantity; PRD and PO answer say Total Qty.
PRD does not say which spelling the message names.
PRD counts inactive copies for the number message, silent for the description message.
Screen not named in the PRD.
PRD silent on which number the warning names when typed and stored numbers differ.
Two PRD messages fit the same situation.
PRD silent on whether cores count.
PRD label differs from today's list.
PRD silent on a punctuation-only change.

The bug asks for historical snapshots to be explicitly addressed but does not say how. The question on available-to-pick (5 Available for +5 and -2) was dropped: SV-10380 says the parts list's available-to-pick quantity keeps its existing behaviour.
Dashboard v1 plan may remove the list before this ships.
